skill.name: safe-edit
skill.description: Guides agents through backups, diff capture, rollback planning, modular implementation, and verification before code changes.
skill.summary: Adds a repeatable safety workflow for reversible code edits.
skill.author: Doyajin174

security_audit.summary: The skill is mostly documentation for a reversible editing workflow, and many command-execution alerts are Markdown false positives. Real concerns remain around writing potentially sensitive diffs to /tmp/diffs, retaining hidden backups, and recommending a destructive Git rollback command.

remediation.suggestion: Use a project-local private directory with restrictive permissions, and warn users before storing sensitive patches.

remediation.issue: Hidden backups can retain sensitive file contents.
remediation.suggestion: Document retention clearly, add cleanup guidance, and ensure backup folders are excluded from commits.

remediation.issue: Rollback examples include git reset --hard HEAD~1.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer safer restore commands, or require status checks and explicit confirmation before destructive Git operations.

remediation.issue: Line-count examples use xargs without null delimiters.
remediation.suggestion: Use null-safe find and xargs patterns to avoid filename parsing issues.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Git Rollback Command
semantic_findings.description: The rollback guidance includes git reset --hard HEAD~1. This can discard local changes and rewrite unpushed history without repository-state checks.

content.user_title: Protect Code Changes with Safe Edit
content.value_statement: Code edits can lose context, overwrite work, or be hard to reverse. Safe Edit adds backups, diffs, rollback notes, modular planning, and verification.
actual_capabilities: Creates timestamped backups before file changes.
Plans rollback methods using backups, patches, or Git.
Checks file length and recommends modularization.
Suggests specialized agents for analysis or implementation.
Tracks multi-step implementation work with TODOs.
limitations: It depends on agent support for Bash, file editing, and task tools.
It can create extra local files that need cleanup.
It does not guarantee tests exist or pass.
It should not replace version control or code review.

use_cases.title: Make Reversible Feature Edits
use_cases.description: Add a feature while keeping backups, diffs, and rollback notes available.

use_cases.title: Review Large Refactors
use_cases.description: Break oversized files into smaller modules and preserve evidence for review.

use_cases.title: Control AI Coding Sessions
use_cases.description: Require structured planning, TODO tracking, and verification before accepting agent changes.

prompt_templates.title: Begin a Safe Edit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a small change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Safe Edit for this change. Back up affected files, save diffs, make the edit, and report verification evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Fix with Rollback Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Fix the issue with Safe Edit. Identify affected files, create backups, save diffs, and include rollback options in the final report.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Large File
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply Safe Edit to refactor this large file. Keep modules under the stated size limits and explain each extracted responsibility.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a Complex Implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Safe Edit for this multi-file implementation. Plan tasks, choose suitable agents if available, back up files, save diffs, test, and summarize risks.

output_examples.input: Add a loading state to the dashboard.
output_examples.output: The response lists backed up files, saved diff locations, the implemented loading state, verification results, and rollback steps.
The response explains the module split, reports new file sizes, notes backups and diffs, and states which checks passed.

output_examples.input: Undo the recent pricing page change.
output_examples.output: The response presents backup restore, patch reversal, and Git-based rollback choices with cautions for destructive actions.

best_practices: Review backups and diffs before accepting a large change.
Store diffs in a project-local private folder when code is sensitive.
Confirm rollback commands before running destructive Git operations.
anti_patterns: Skipping backups because a change seems small.
Saving sensitive diffs in shared temporary folders.
Using destructive rollback commands without checking repository state.

faq.question: What does Safe Edit do before changing files?
faq.answer: It plans the task, backs up affected files, saves diffs, and prepares rollback guidance.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: It recommends type checks and builds when applicable, but available project commands still determine what can run.

faq.question: Where are backups stored by default?
faq.answer: The skill describes project-local backups under a hidden backup folder.

faq.question: Where are diffs stored by default?
faq.answer: The source documents a temporary diff folder, which should be changed for sensitive projects.

faq.question: Can it replace Git?
faq.answer: No. It complements Git with local backups, patch files, and rollback notes.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Developers and AI coding operators who want reversible edits and clearer implementation records.
